chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
He said: The habitual drinker of wine will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when he meets Him, like an idol worshipper.

key_terms.يَلْقَى اللَّهَ: To meet Allah (on the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a habitual wine drinker on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from the Imams to establish that habitual wine consumption constitutes a major sin that alters one's spiritual ontology, equating the drinker's state before Allah to that of a polytheist (mushrik). This comparison underscores the concept of *khamr* not merely as a physical intoxicant but as a veil that obscures divine recognition, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence linking ritual purity to theological monotheism. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding how habitual sin can lead to a form of practical idolatry by displacing God's centrality in the believer's consciousness.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:
‘The habitual (drinker of) the wine would meet Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic when he meets Him<sup>azwj</sup> like an idol worshipper’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
A wine addict will meet Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, when he will meet Him, as a worshipper of idols will do.’”
